Horsehead Corporation was a U.S.-based metals and chemical enterprise historically associated with zinc production, zinc recycling, and related value‑added products used across a wide range of industrial supply chains. With corporate operations long tied to **300 Frankfort Road, Monaca, Pennsylvania 15061-2295**, the company became particularly well known for its role in **recovering zinc from industrial byproducts**, most notably electric-arc furnace (EAF) dust generated by steelmakers. By transforming these residual materials into usable zinc-bearing feedstocks and products, Horsehead positioned itself at the intersection of heavy industry and resource recovery, serving customers in galvanizing, steel, rubber, agriculture, and chemical manufacturing.

Over time, Horsehead’s business model emphasized both **primary zinc production** and **recycling-based production**, reflecting a broader trend in the chemical and metals sectors toward efficiency and circular-material strategies. Zinc and zinc compounds are essential inputs for corrosion protection (especially galvanized steel), alloying, and numerous chemical applications, and Horsehead’s operations aimed to supply consistent, specification-grade material for these end uses while managing complex feedstocks and regulatory requirements.

It is also important to note that Horsehead underwent significant corporate changes in the mid‑2010s, including financial restructuring and subsequent ownership transitions. Even so, the company’s name remains closely associated with the Monaca address and with the industrial legacy of zinc recovery and processing in the region.
